The mixture is reacted with a chemical reagent that selectively reacts with one component, leaving the others unchanged. An example is the titration of an acid with a base to determine its concentration.

Distillation is a process in which a mixture is separated into its components based on their solubility in a solvent. The mixture is dissolved in a solvent, and the soluble components are separated from the insoluble ones. An example is the extraction of caffeine from coffee beans.

Distillation is a process in which a mixture is separated into its components based on their density. The mixture is allowed to settle, and the denser components sink to the bottom, while the lighter ones remain on top. An example is the separation of sand and water.
